issue_context.title: Max result incorrect when using Unsigned bigint as primary key.
issue_context.body:
## Bug Report

Please answer these questions before submitting your issue. Thanks!

1. What did you do?
If possible, provide a recipe for reproducing the error.
```
create table test_uint64(c1 bigint unsigned, primary key(c1));
insert into test_uint64 values(9223372036854775807);
insert into test_uint64 values(18446744073709551615);
select max(c1) from test_uint64;
```

2. What did you expect to see?
```
mysql> select max(c1) from test_uint64;
+----------------------+
| max(c1)              |
+----------------------+
| 18446744073709551615 |
+----------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```

3. What did you see instead?
```
mysql> select max(c1) from test_uint64;
+---------------------+
| max(c1)             |
+---------------------+
| 9223372036854775807 |
+---------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec)
```


4. What version of TiDB are you using (`tidb-server -V` or run `select tidb_version();` on TiDB)?

Any version will do.
comments:
One more thing to add is that max works as expected on pk is not handle case

```
CREATE TABLE `test_uint642` (
  `c1` bigint(20) UNSIGNED DEFAULT NULL,
  `c2` char(10) DEFAULT NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB DEFAULT CHARSET=utf8mb4 COLLATE=utf8mb4_bin``` 

 mysql> insert into test_uint642 values(18446744073709551615, "edeededede");
Query OK, 1 row affected (0.01 sec)

mysql> select max(c1) from test_uint642;
+----------------------+
| max(c1)              |
+----------------------+
| 18446744073709551615 |
+----------------------+
1 row in set (0.01 sec) 
```
I think it is an known issue, because the handle must be signed.

Supplement:
```
mysql> select c1 from test_uint64 where c1 > 9223372036854775807;
ERROR 1105 (HY000): other error: unknown error StringError("[src/coprocessor/dag/executor/table_scan.rs:60]: invalid range,range.start should be smaller than range.end, but got [[116, 128, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 7, 95, 114, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 0],[116, 128, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, 2, 7, 95, 114, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 255, 0])")
```
The range should be dealt correctly on borders.
@XuHuaiyu I've fixed it. Adding tests now.

review_comments:
It should be another separate problem.
Before split ranges, it's already become `(9223372036854775808,+inf]`.

Yes... I just have tried this SQL in master branch and it has the same problem...
I will create a new issue for this problem.
Why do we need this check?
Because there can be cases like `(maxInt64, maxInt64]` and [maxInt64+1, maxInt64+1)`. And then error thrown when send requests.
